chapter: Becoming a musician: ukulele, clarinet and the Boozaire Kings
title: Clarinet lessons with Barney Bigard and kids practicing everywhere
summary: Paul sent him to Barney Bigard for clarinet lessons while Don Albert and Herman Henderson also took lessons nearby.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: So he sent me to Barney Bigard. They were working at ...(?)... So I went to see Barney Bigard, and he gave me a little book, and I started figuring out them notes -- and they still all, some of them, the same to me today. So I worked with him for about what...about three months -- when I could catch him. But my God, he would sit down and play
Now, he must have lived in another part of town, too, didn't he?
Lived right around a couple of blocks from me.

Now, across the street from me is Don Albert, who is going to school taking clarinet lessons. And on the next block is Herman Henderson. He's taking clarinet lessons. And all around you, every day you could hear horns. You'd pass the street and listen to some kid practicing a horn, practicing the clarinet, or somebody playing the piano. It was just music, music, music, music, music, music, music. No football, no basketball, no nothin'. It was nothing else but music. So little Herman Henderson, he showed me how to get them three chords, the foundation, and how to sing, and to get the song "Chinaman and Mabel."
